title: Excel for Beginners: Learn the Excel Skills You Actually Use at Work, One Real Task a Day
description: You said you know Excel. Now you have to hand in a file by Friday. Stop watching tutorials. Time to practice. The Task Ladder method to actually learn how to use Excel. You said you know Excel. Now you have to hand in a spreadsheet by Friday, and you’re staring at rows and columns with no idea where to click first. Sound familiar? Do you really think another evening of pausing tutorials every ten seconds will help, when you’re the one who has to finish that file? Here’s the problem: watching someone else use Excel isn’t the same as using it yourself . And memorizing functions doesn’t teach you which one to pick when a real task lands on your desk. You don’t need one more explanation. You need to finish something with your own hands . That’s what the Task Ladder is for: a hands-on 7-day method where every real task you complete prepares you for the next one. On day one you start from a very simple sheet. Step by step, each rung builds on what you did the day before, always on real work tasks. In 7 days you’ll be analyzing data and building a chart that looks great, and you’ll know exactly how you got there. Created by Leonard Webb, a computer engineer with 26 years of Excel experience , Excel for Beginners is a 7-day path built around 7 practice files , one for each day, free to download. Over 200 illustrated screenshots walk you through one task at a time, so you always know where you are and where to click next. Here’s what you’ll discover inside: How to turn 120 rows of raw sales data into a PivotTable and a chart you can explain with confidence in Monday’s meeting, after just 7 days of practice.
